questions.question: When was the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) established in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1927**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI)** is a non-profit trade organization and lobbying organization located in India.
 
• In 1927, Indian businessmen Mr. G D Birla and Purshottamdas Thakurdas launched the company on Mahatma Gandhi's recommendation.
 
• It is India's largest, most influential, and oldest commercial organization.
 
• It is a non-governmental, non-profit organization. Members of FICCI come from the private and public sectors, as well as SMEs and multinational enterprises.
 
• The chamber has around 250,000 indirect members through a variety of regional chambers of commerce.
 
• It focuses on firm development, advertising, and networking in a given industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• It is based in New Delhi, India's capital, and operates in 12 states and eight countries worldwide.
 
• India's only national ATA Carnet issuing and assuring organization is the FICCI.
 
• ATA Carnets are used to carry temporary equipment across borders by TV/film crews, journalists, engineers, musicians, and industry.

questions.question: Sardar Sarovar Dam is situated in the state of _______ and on the river _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Gujarat, Narmada__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **On the Indian Narmada River, the Sardar Sarovar Dam (SSD) is located in the village of Kevadia in Gujarat.**
 
• It is one of the country's largest and most contentious multipurpose river valley infrastructure development projects.
 
• Auxiliary works including a 1,450MW power complex are also part of the Sardar Sarovar Project (SSP).
 
• In 2010-2011, SSP was expected to have cost INR400 billion, up from an initial estimate of INR64 billion in 1988.
 
• It is part of the Narmada Valley Development Project, a large-scale project to generate electricity and provide drinking and irrigation water to the states of Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Narmada River is India's fifth longest river, the largest west-flowing river, and the largest flowing river in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat states of India share this river.
 
• Because of its various contributions to the states of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, it is also known as "Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat's Lifeline."

questions.question: How many monasteries and temples are there in Ellora caves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__34__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ellora Caves** are a series of 34 monasteries and temples that were dug side by side in the wall of a steep basalt cliff near Aurangabad, Maharashtra.
 
• Ellora, with its continuous line of monuments ranging from 600 to 1000 A.D., brings ancient India's civilization to life.
 
• The Ellora complex is not only a one-of-a-kind aesthetic and technological achievement, but it also exemplifies ancient India's tolerant attitude, with sanctuaries dedicated to Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism.
 
• Through extraordinary architectural activities carried out by adherents of three significant religions: Buddhism, Brahmanism, and Jainism, the unique ensemble of 34 caves at Ellora in the Charanandri hills of western India's Maharashtra State display a spirit of coexistence and religious tolerance.
 
• From the sixth through the twelfth centuries, rock-cutting took place in three stages.

questions.question: A file with the _______ file extension is a Word Open XML Macro-Enabled Document file.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**.docm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **A Word Open XML Macro-Enabled Document file with the DOCM extension is used in Microsoft Word.**
 
• It first appeared in Office 2007. DOCM files are similar to DOCX files, but they can also run macros, allowing you to automate repetitive activities in Word.
 
• DOCM files, like DOCX files, can store formatted text, pictures, shapes, charts, and other data.
 
• This format, like Microsoft's other XML formats like DOCX and XLSX, employs XML and ZIP to compress data into a smaller size.
 
• The primary software tool for opening and editing DOCM files is Microsoft Word (version 2007 and higher).

questions.question: Which of the following states leads in sunflower cultivation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Six states produce the majority of the country's sunflowers, with Karnataka leading the way.**
 
• Karnataka, with a production of 3.04 lakh tonnes from an area of 7.94 lakh hectares, is India's largest sunflower producer, followed by Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, Orissa, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• Sunflower agriculture covers around 1.48 million hectares in India, with an average yield of 0.6 metric tonnes per acre.
 
• Because around 80% of the region is under rain-fed agriculture, sunflower production is subject to systemic weather risk.
 
• Bihar leads the way in terms of productivity with 1402 kg/ha, followed by Tamil Nadu with 1328.7 kg, despite the fact that both states have fewer than 25000 hectares under the crop, which is primarily irrigated.
 
• The sunflower crop takes 90-100 days to mature. When the lower half of the head turns yellow and some of the bracts dry up, the crop must be picked.

questions.question: A large area of land demarcated as Damin-i-Koh in 1832 was declared as the land of the _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Santhals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A large area of land demarcated as** Damin-i-Koh** in 1832 was declared as the land of the **Santhals**.
 
• The government set aside a big area in Damin-i-Koh for the Santals' habitation in 1832.
 
• This tract's population grew from 3,000 in 1838 to 82,795 in 1851.
 
• Damin-i-Koh was the name given to the forested steep portions of the Rajmahal Hills in the present-day districts of Sahebganj, Pakur, and Godda in Jharkhand, India.
 
• In eastern India, the Santals are the most populous group.
 
• The 1793 Permanent Settlement compelled landowners to increase land productivity.
